name: Affordable / LIHTC multifamily
summary: Income-restricted new-construction rental financed with 9% or 4% LIHTC, usually garden or mid-rise. Hard costs per SF run above market-rate (smaller units, durability/green standards, accessibility, community space, sometimes prevailing wage) and soft costs are much heavier (syndication, legal, developer fee, reserves). Strong public data: Florida Housing's 2026 hard-cost-per-unit factors by building type, RAND's LIHTC vs market-rate cost decomposition for TX/CO/CA, and California TCAC-based TDC medians; national hard-cost averages are older.

typicalSize.method: 9% deals commonly 50-100 units (Florida's TDC template has '=<50 Units' and '51-80 Units' multipliers for 9% NC); 4% bond deals 150-300. Mid 100.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross SF per unit incl. community/service space; LIHTC unit mixes are smaller than market-rate on average (RAND) but family deals carry 2-3BR units; Census median new rental unit 1,000 net SF (e15).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Garden deals ~16-30 units/acre (see garden-multifamily.json); urban mid-rise LIHTC 40-80+. Mid reflects the garden/mid-rise mix.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Typical suburban family LIHTC 1.5-2.0 surface spaces/unit; senior and urban deals 0.5-1.0 (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Mid anchored on Florida Housing's 2026/27 new-construction hard-cost-per-unit factors (e1-e4): garden $256-284k, mid-rise $284-311k, high-rise $338k outside South Florida. Those are ceilings, so the national typical (garden/mid-rise mix) mid is set at ~$255k, in line with Terrapin's LIHTC range $240-380k (e13). RAND 2019 per-NRSF hard costs (TX $173, CO $183, CA $427; e6-e8) show LIHTC at ~1.5x Texas market rate per SF and the large California premium; low = Sun Belt garden 4% deal, high = coastal/prevailing-wage mid-rise (California LIHTC TDCs ~$555-573k/unit, e11).

perSF.method: perPrimaryUnit / sfPerPrimaryUnit (1,000 GSF): mid ~$255/GSF, low ~$195 (185k/950), high ~$380 (400k/1,050). Cross-check: RAND LIHTC hard per NRSF (2019 $) TX $173 / CO $183 / CA $427 (e6-e8) - roughly 1.0-1.5x the market-rate garden per-SF in the same markets.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general requirements, overhead and profit (HFA-capped builder fees), on-site work and community building; excludes land, soft costs, developer fee, reserves, FF&E, off-sites, impact/tap fees and financing. Mid-rise/podium LIHTC with structured parking should use the podium file's parking items.

qualityTiers.method: LIHTC specifications are standardized by HFA design standards, so the spread is narrower than market-rate; Florida's ESSC (concrete/masonry) vs non-ESSC garden factor is +11% (e1) and mid-rise ESSC vs non-ESSC +10% (e2).

systemSplit.method: Derived: 60% garden split (sourced from RAND Table 3.4 Texas garden data, see garden-multifamily.json) + 40% podium split (derived, see podium-multifamily.json), reflecting the garden/mid-rise mix of new-construction LIHTC; division 01 absorbs rounding.

lineItems.name: Community room / resident services and leasing space

cost.method: Derived: 2,000-4,000 SF community/services building or ground-floor space required by most QAPs, at ~$250-375/SF (2026).

lineItems.name: Prevailing wage (Davis-Bacon / state) premium

cost.method: Derived: Davis-Bacon (HOME/HUD funds) or state prevailing wage typically adds ~5-15% to hard cost outside California (~$12-38k on the $255k mid); UCLA estimates ~$100,000 per unit in California (e12) as the high end.

lineItems.notes: Switch on when federal/state funds or local rules trigger prevailing wage.

lineItems.name: Green building / energy certification requirements (EGC, NGBS, ENERGY STAR)

cost.method: Derived: incremental envelope, mechanical and verification costs to meet QAP green standards ~1-4% of hard cost (2026 judgment).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; most QAPs require a green standard.

cost.method: Derived: roll-in showers, lowered counters, grab bars, wider clearances for ~5-10% of units (2026 judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: community room, computer lab, fitness and office furniture/equipment ~ $100-250k per deal (2026).

pctOfHard.method: Florida's TDC cap implies soft = 1/3 of hard before developer fee (e5); RAND LIHTC soft/hard 0.35 (TX), 0.41 (CO), 0.44 (CA) including financing and developer costs (e9). Mid 0.33 excludes developer fee and construction interest; low = lean 4% bond deal, high = coastal 9% deal with layered public funding.

softCosts.notes: Model the developer fee separately (Florida caps it at 16% of non-acquisition development cost; other states ~12-15%). Add tax-credit syndication, bond issuance, reserves (operating/replacement) and HFA fees as LIHTC-specific soft items.

developerFee.method: Derived from the state caps in this file’s soft-cost note: Florida caps the developer fee at 16% of non-acquisition development cost, other states ~12–15%; mid 12%.

hard.method: Derived: HFAs commonly require/allow 5% (rehab higher) hard contingency; investors/lenders often push 5-10% for new construction.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $185k x 1.25 ~= $230k; hard high $400k x 1.6 (heavy soft + dev fee + contingency) ~= $640k, extended to $750k to admit California prevailing-wage deals (TCAC median TDC ~$555-573k incl. land in 2018-24 dollars, e11). Abt/NCSHA median TDC $164,757 (2011-16, e10) shows how far costs have risen.
